title: Automatic brightness for keyboard (enable while typing, adjust with ambiend light sensor)
line: The keyboard backlight can now turn off by itself when you stop typing, and in bright light on laptops with a light sensor.
explanation: Power management could only set a fixed keyboard backlight level per power profile; nothing turned it off while the keyboard wasn't used, and the ambient light sensor (which KWin already uses for screen brightness) was ignored for the keyboard. Each power profile now has a "Turn off keyboard backlight" idle timeout (Never by default, 5 s to 5 min or custom): the backlight goes off after that much inactivity and comes back at its previous level on the next key press or mouse move. When iio-sensor-proxy reports an ambient light sensor, a "Turn off keyboard backlight in bright light" checkbox also appears; powerdevil then claims the sensor and turns the backlight off above 300 lux and back on below 150 lux.

commits.message:
daemon, kcm: turn off keyboard backlight when idle or in bright light

The keyboard backlight stayed on no matter whether the user was typing
or how bright the room was. Power profiles can now turn it off after a
chosen idle time and, when a light sensor is present, in bright light.

BUG: 516629

media.caption: Before: Power Management only offers a fixed keyboard brightness per profile.
After: new "Turn off keyboard backlight" idle timeout and, with a light sensor, a bright-light checkbox.
After: idle timeout choices for the keyboard backlight.

review.text: The idle-timeout part is sound and fits the existing per-profile action and idle-timeout infrastructure. The ambient-light part adds a second iio-sensor-proxy client with hard-coded 300/150 lux thresholds inside the keyboard action, and the KCM blocks on a synchronous system-bus call in load(). Bundling both in one 300-line commit makes it hard for powerdevil maintainers to review or accept either part.
changes: Split into two commits/MRs: the keyboard backlight idle timeout first, the bright-light option separately.

In PowerKCM::load(), don't make a blocking system-bus call to net.hadess.SensorProxy (it can trigger D-Bus activation); query HasAmbientLight asynchronously and update the property when the reply arrives.

For the bright-light part, coordinate with KWin's existing ambient-light handling (it already claims the sensor for screen brightness), or at least justify the fixed lux thresholds in the MR, rather than adding an independent sensor client with magic numbers.
